newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NMFM ASIA PROPOSES RESTRUCTURE INTO TRUST.
newsitem.headline: NMFM ASIA PROPOSES RESTRUCTURE INTO TRUST.

text.p: NMFM Asia Investments said on Thursday it was proposing to shareholders and optionholders a restructure of the company into an open ended trust with units and options listing on the Australian and New Zealand stock exchanges.
"This would result in the company becoming a listed 'variable capital' entity," the company said in a statement, adding it had already had preliminary discussions with the ASX about the proposal.

"While there are aspects of the proposal which need to be worked through in detail, the ASX has given its in principle agreement to the reconstruction and the to various attributes of the variable capital entity," it said.
The proposed reconstruction will have two key features --
1. The introduction of a Periodic Redemption Facility referenced to the underlying Net Tangible Assets (NTA) per unit of the trust.
2. The introduction of a Continuous Issue Facility.

"The Directors of the company believe that the introduction of a Periodic Redemption Facility would significantly reduce the current discount that exists between the company's NTA per share and its share price.
"This should therefore allow the company's underlying investments to be reflected in the value of the shares listed on the ASX and NZSE," the company said.
A Continuous Issue Facility would give investors flexibility to increase their investment in the trust.

"Equally, the Continuous Issue Facility would give the trust flexibility to raise additional funds to take advantage of new investment opportunities within the Asian region, as defined in the company's prospectus," NMFM said.
The underlying objectives and activities of the company would not change following the reconstruction of the company into a trust.
NMFM shares last traded in New Zealand at NZ$1.09 per share, up three cents.
